inputs.xtext_rule_text:
TriggerExpression returns SysML::TriggerInvocationExpression :
	  kind = TimeTriggerKind
	  ownedRelationship += ArgumentMember
	| kind = ChangeTriggerKind
	  ownedRelationship += ArgumentExpressionMember
;

notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: SysML 8.2.2.17.4 states this production, but prints `kind = ( 'at | 'after' )` with no closing quote after at, so read literally the first literal never terminates and no rule can be derived. The quote is closed: the intended literals are 'at' and 'after', which the clause's own correctly-spelled 'when' beside them and the pilot grammar both confirm. Recorded as the deviation TriggerExpression, follow_spec; the defect is filed as SYSML21-401, open. Otherwise the clause is transcribed. The `kind =` assignments contribute no tokens, and the Xtext reaches the same three literals through two enums, TimeTriggerKind `'at' | 'after'` (SysML.xtext:1479) and ChangeTriggerKind `'when'` (1483) — the same device it uses for Expose's visibility and the transition feature kinds. The two branches differ in more than their keyword: a time trigger takes an ArgumentMember and a change trigger an ArgumentExpressionMember, which is the laziness distinction — the change trigger wraps its value in a reference so the expression is re-evaluated rather than evaluated once.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription with the unterminated literal closed.
Why the first literal reads 'at' rather than running to the next quote.
Open. 'TriggerExpression missing closing quote after 'at'. Page fetched and body read on 2026-09-17.

Line 18 `then accept sig after 10[SI::s];` takes 'after' with an ArgumentMember. Line 19 `then accept at new Time::Iso8601DateTime("2022-01-30T01:00:00Z");` takes 'at'. Line 22 `then accept when b.f;` takes the change branch with an ArgumentExpressionMember.
Second opinion. Same three literals once TimeTriggerKind (1479) and ChangeTriggerKind (1483) are unwound.
